chapter: Mario Bauza and the Cuban sextets
title: Playing with Sexteto Agabama
summary: He joined Barroso's Agabama with Cheo Marquetti and Felix Chapotin, playing son montuno, which he says is now called salsa.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Abelardo Barroso, the vocalist, he had a group called La Agabama?
Agabama, and Cheo Marqueti, a great singer too, was a bass player.
Cheo Marqueti played bass for La Agabama?
Yes
WOW!
Yeah! Oh, there was a cyclone, that sextet! and I loved it because it was so tipico.
How many men were in The Agabama?
The Agabama was Barroso, Cheo Marqueti, the bongo player, the guitar player, the tres player and Chapotin in the trumpet.
Felix Chapotin was in that group too?
Yes, he was our trumpet.
What year was this?
WOW! four legends. You, Marqueti, Barroso and Chapotin.
And Chapotin.
And - and Agabama, What kind of music were you playing then?
Son - ah - eh - the same that.......
Afro-Cuban son? El son montuno?
Yeah, what they call it salsa now.
I see.
All the numbers that we used to sing fifty years ago I hear now like it's something new, but what can you tell?
I see. Okay, Where did you work?
Well, we worked all those clubs, like you say Corso or Casablanca, whatever, you know, public places.
But were they called clubs then?
Not particularly, there was like incorporated club, they used to give dances at the Tropicana or at the Cerveza Tropical place, there was like a center.
Side 2, cassette 1.
